title: If July’s stretch of dominance wasn’t enough, the Red Sox’ win Friday proved they’re plenty capable of a postseason run
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Boston Red Sox defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-4 on Friday, showcasing their postseason potential.
Ceddanne Rafaela's late-game heroics and solid team efforts highlighted the Red Sox's victory despite key injuries.
The Red Sox approach the trade deadline in strong form, outperforming expectations from earlier in the season.

title: Red Sox fend off Dodgers, 9-4, in grindy series opener
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh inning, leading the Red Sox to a 9-4 win.
Brayan Bello pitched four scoreless innings in relief, improving his bullpen ERA to 0.69 and earning the win.
The Red Sox ended July with a franchise-best 21-4 record, boosting their playoff prospects with the victory.

title: Gabe Jacas makes his Patriots debut and other takeaways from Day 7 of training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Gabe Jacas made his practice debut for the Patriots on Saturday in a limited role after recovering from a knee procedure.
The Patriots' defense secured two interceptions during training camp's third-straight padded practice in Foxborough.
Undrafted free agent Tanner Arkin is gaining attention for his blocking skills and solid performance during team drills.

title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts will distribute chip-enabled EBT cards statewide to prevent fraud and theft, impacting nearly 1 million SNAP recipients.
The transition follows a successful pilot program in Worcester and is supported by 2025 legislative funding approval.
Recipients must activate new cards within 60 days; retailers are updating systems to accept chip or tap payments.

title: Boston is now offering ‘pet certificates’ for couples who wed at City Hall
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston City Hall now offers 'pet certificates' for couples marrying there, recognizing pets as family members.
Mayor Michelle Wu announced the program, emphasizing the importance of pets in shared commitment and household love.
The first pet certificate was awarded to Bono, a golden retriever, during a City Hall wedding officiated by Paul Chong.

title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon will perform stand-up shows in Boston and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, this week.
Nealon's comedic style incorporates absurd tweets and his experiences as an 'old dad' in his special 'Loose in the Crotch.'
The comedian hosts a YouTube show, 'Hiking with Kevin,' where he conducts interviews while hiking with guests.

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox catcher Willson Contreras was hit by a 95 MPH pitch from Dodgers pitcher Will Klein on Friday.
Contreras stayed in the game briefly after the incident but was later removed for precautionary reasons.
Contreras leads the Red Sox in multiple batting categories and his condition will be reassessed Saturday.

title: After Patriots coaching stint, DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech staff
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech as an assistant wide receivers coach after a stint at Patriots training camp.
Hopkins, 34, gains praise from New England players during training camp before deciding to pursue coaching.
Georgia Tech head coach David Key values Hopkins's leadership and familiarity with offensive strategies.

title: Could Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both make the Patriots 53-man roster?
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are competing for spots on the Patriots' 53-man roster.
New England Patriots currently have seven wide receivers vying for six typical NFL roster spots.
Drake Maye shows strong connections with his wide receivers during the Patriots' training camp.

title: Reports: OF George Springer interested in trade to Red Sox, team eyeing INF Xavier Edwards
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: George Springer is open to a trade to the Boston Red Sox despite having an eight-team no-trade list.
The Red Sox are interested in Miami Marlins infielder Xavier Edwards, who fits their need for infield help.
Springer, currently with the Blue Jays, and Edwards are both associated with trade rumors involving the Red Sox.
